  5. Chemical energetics

  10. Chemistry of the environment

Papers: Paper 1 (Core) or Paper 2 (Extended), 40 multiple-choice questions, 45 min; Paper 3 (Core) or Paper 4 (Extended), theory, 1 h 15 min, 80 marks; Paper 5 (practical test, 1 h 15 min, 40 marks) or Paper 6 (alternative to practical, 1 h, 40 marks). Unit 1 of 10: Solids, Liquids and Gases

Key ideas

  • Solid: particles closely packed in a regular arrangement, vibrating about fixed positions; fixed shape and volume.
  • Liquid: particles close together, irregular, moving past one another; fixed volume, takes the container's shape.
  • Gas: particles far apart, random, moving fast; no fixed shape or volume; can be compressed.
  • (S) Gas volume depends on temperature and pressure: higher temperature increases the volume; higher pressure decreases it.

Worked examples

Example 1: a gas can be compressed because there is lots of space between its particles.

Example 2: a liquid flows because its particles can move past each other.

Example 3 (S): a sealed balloon left in the sun expands, because its gas particles move faster and push outwards more.

10-mark exam-style question

(a) Describe the arrangement and motion of particles in each state. [6] (b) Explain why gases are easily compressed. [2] (c) (S) Explain why a gas syringe's volume increases when heated at constant pressure. [2]

Answers: (a) Solid: regular, close, vibrate; liquid: random, close, slide past; gas: random, far apart, fast and random (B6). (b) The particles are far apart, with space between them. (c) The particles gain kinetic energy and move faster, hitting the plunger harder and more often, pushing it out.

Common mistakes

  1. Saying solid particles do not move. 2. Saying particles expand when heated. 3. Liquids drawn with gaps like gases. 4. Mixing "volume" and "shape". 5. Vague particle language.

Quick recall

  1. Which state has a fixed shape? 2. Which can be compressed? 3. Motion in a solid? 4. Effect of pressure on gas volume (S)? 5. Which state flows but has a fixed volume?

Answers: 1) Solid. 2) Gas. 3) Vibration. 4) Volume decreases. 5) Liquid.
